prompt: Which items does OSIsoft training say a Data Archive backup plan must cover? Select all that apply.

options.text: Data files: snapshot, event queues, archives
Configuration: point configuration and tuning parameters
The subsystems (Windows services) and the hardware underneath
Only the newest archive file

explanation: The training lists subsystems, data files (snapshot, event queues, archives), configuration (point configuration, tuning parameters) and the hardware. Backing up only one archive loses the rest.

scenario: Ransomware encrypts a PI server's disks. The nightly PI backup was written to D:\PIBackup on the same server and nowhere else.
prompt: Which practice from AVEVA's 2023 security guidance would have prevented the loss?

options.text: A two-phase strategy: back up locally first, then copy to a separate server
Running backups during peak hours
Disabling VSS
Using larger archive files

explanation: AVEVA recommends daily incremental backups off-peak with Task Scheduler and a two-phase strategy (local first, then a copy to a separate server). Keeping backups only on the same server is a listed mistake.

prompt: Match each piartool -backup option to what it selects.

pairs.right: The latest n archives counted back from now

explanation: piartool -backup supports -numarch and -archives; it cannot take a range of older archives (AVEVA feedback portal PIDA-1092).

prompt: Which Windows service lets PI backups copy files that are in use? Give its name or acronym.
explanation: PI backups use the Windows Volume Shadow Copy Service (VSS), so they can back up files in use without downtime.

prompt: When PIBackup.bat calls AFBackup.bat, what does the AF SQL backup run?

options.text: The stored procedure dbo.usp_backup on the PIFD database
piartool -backup -numarch 1
pidiag -archk on the AF database
A copy of piarcmem.dat

explanation: The AF SQL backup runs dbo.usp_backup on PIFD, for example sqlcmd -S <instance> -d PIFD -Q "EXEC dbo.usp_backup @outpath = N'<path>';" -E.

prompt: How much free space does a rollback backup during a PI Server upgrade need?

options.text: Space equal to the databases plus the primary archive
Space equal to all registered archives
10 MB
None; rollback backups are stored in memory

explanation: The architecture workbook says a rollback backup during upgrades needs space equal to the databases plus the primary archive.

prompt: True or false: according to AVEVA's 2019 architecture talk, PI backups, redundant interfaces and high availability are complete disaster-recovery solutions on their own.

options.text: True
False

explanation: The talk states they are NOT stand-alone disaster-recovery solutions, and recommends a DR simulation at least once a year.

prompt: A team wants to restore last night's backup to a spare server and keep it running as a hot standby. What does the 2026 licence schedule say?

options.text: Backup copies may not be used as a hot standby, for testing or training, or as a caching server
Backup copies may run as hot standby for up to 90 days
Any backup copy may run as a hot standby
Hot standby is allowed only for PI Test Servers

explanation: The schedule forbids using backup copies for testing or training, as a hot standby or as a caching server. HA uses licensed collective members.

prompt: Order the steps of AVEVA's recommended daily backup routine.

items.text: Windows Task Scheduler starts the backup off-peak
The backup is copied to a separate server

explanation: AVEVA recommends daily incremental backups off-peak with Windows Task Scheduler, local first, then a copy to a separate server.

prompt: How does PI Collective Manager bring a new secondary member up to date with history?

options.text: It takes a PI Backup of the primary, copies it and registers it on the secondary
It replicates every event from the primary in real time
It reprocesses the secondary's archives offline
It asks interfaces to resend all history

explanation: Per PI Square, PI Collective Manager synchronises a secondary by taking a PI Backup of the primary, copying it and registering it.
